simple.meaning: חָגָב (châgâb) is a Hebrew word meaning “a locust.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: חָגָב (H2284) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Leviticus 11:22, with occurrences in Leviticus, Numbers, 2 Chronicles, Ecclesiastes, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָגָב (H2284) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in חָגָב (H2284) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: חָגָב (châgâb) / H2284 is traced through Leviticus 11:22, Numbers 13:33, 2 Chronicles 7:13, Ecclesiastes 12:5 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H2284. chagab I. חָגָב noun masculine Eccl 12:5 locust, grasshopper (Late Hebrew id. ; compare ᵑ7 ), probably a non-flying species, see Kn in Di Lev 11:22 ; הֶחָגָב allowed as food 11:22 (P; || חַרְגֹּל סָלְעָם, אַרְבֶּה, ), כַּחֲגָבִיס Num 13:33 (J E; simile of insignificance), so Isa 40:22 ; as agent of Yahweh's wrath חארץ לֶאֱכוֺל חָגָב 2Chr 7:13 ; הֶחָגָב וְיִסְתַּבֵּל Eccl 12:5 and the grasshopper shall be a burden ; better shall drag itself along , De Hi Now RVm; De thinks ׳ח here figurative of the back part of the pelvic cavity (Arabic is point of hip-bone , Bo, compare Lane), and refers to stiffness of aged joints, so Now; but the meaning is dubious; see other views of Comm.
